questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health economics, insurance, Ayushman Bharat & financing
questions.stem: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana provides health cover of:
options: Five lakh rupees per family per year for secondary and tertiary hospitalisation
questions.concept: It targets the poorest 40% of the population identified by deprivation criteria, is cashless and paperless at empanelled hospitals, and is portable across states.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health economics, insurance, Ayushman Bharat & financing
questions.stem: The two components of Ayushman Bharat are:
options: Health and Wellness Centres for comprehensive primary care and PM-JAY for hospitalisation
questions.concept: The two pillars address different levels: HWCs deliver 12 packages of comprehensive primary care including NCD screening, while PM-JAY protects against catastrophic hospitalisation expenditure.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health economics, insurance, Ayushman Bharat & financing
questions.stem: Catastrophic health expenditure is conventionally defined as out-of-pocket spending exceeding:
options: Ten percent of total household consumption expenditure
questions.concept: India has among the highest out-of-pocket shares globally, pushing millions below the poverty line annually - the impoverishment effect that health financing reform seeks to prevent.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health economics, insurance, Ayushman Bharat & financing
questions.stem: Cost-effectiveness analysis compares interventions using:
options: Cost per unit of health outcome, such as cost per life year gained
questions.concept: Cost-utility analysis uses QALYs or DALYs allowing comparison across diseases, while cost-benefit analysis values outcomes in money terms, which is ethically contentious for health.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health economics, insurance, Ayushman Bharat & financing
questions.stem: The Employees State Insurance Scheme is financed by:
options: Contributions from employers and employees, making it a social insurance model
questions.concept: Social insurance is compulsory and contributory with risk pooling, distinguishing it from tax-funded national health services and from voluntary private insurance based on individual risk rating.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health economics, insurance, Ayushman Bharat & financing
questions.stem: Moral hazard in health insurance refers to:
options: Increased use of services because the insured does not bear the full cost
questions.concept: Co-payments and gatekeeping mitigate it. Adverse selection is the opposite problem, where those expecting to need care are most likely to insure, which universal enrolment prevents.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health economics, insurance, Ayushman Bharat & financing
questions.stem: The largest share of health expenditure in India has historically been:
questions.concept: Although the out-of-pocket share has fallen with expanded insurance and free service delivery, it remains high, which is why financial protection is a central objective of health policy.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health economics, insurance, Ayushman Bharat & financing
questions.stem: A DALY averted is used in health economics to measure:
options: The health gain from an intervention, combining premature mortality and disability
questions.concept: Interventions are ranked by cost per DALY averted, allowing comparison between, say, immunisation and dialysis. Immunisation and tobacco control are consistently among the most cost-effective.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health economics, insurance, Ayushman Bharat & financing
questions.stem: Strategic purchasing in health financing means:
options: Actively selecting what services to buy, from whom and how to pay, rather than passive budgeting
questions.concept: Provider payment mechanisms - capitation, case-based bundled payment and performance-linked payment - shape provider behaviour, which is why payment design matters as much as the level of funding.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Health economics, insurance, Ayushman Bharat & financing
questions.stem: Rashtriya Swasthya Bima Yojana, the predecessor of PM-JAY, differed principally in:
options: Providing a much lower annual cover of thirty thousand rupees per family
questions.concept: The low cover proved inadequate for serious illness, and evaluations showed limited reduction in out-of-pocket spending - the evidence that drove the far larger PM-JAY entitlement.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Zoonoses: rabies, plague, leptospirosis, brucellosis
questions.stem: India accounts for a large share of global rabies deaths, with the principal reservoir being:
questions.concept: Dog bites cause the overwhelming majority of human rabies in India. Mass dog vaccination achieving 70% coverage, alongside population management, is the only route to elimination.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Zoonoses: rabies, plague, leptospirosis, brucellosis
questions.stem: A category II rabies exposure, defined as minor scratches without bleeding, requires:
options: Wound washing and vaccine, but not immunoglobulin
questions.concept: Category I is touching or feeding with intact skin needing no prophylaxis; category III with transdermal bites, bleeding scratches or mucosal contamination requires immunoglobulin as well as vaccine.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Zoonoses: rabies, plague, leptospirosis, brucellosis
questions.stem: Wound washing after an animal bite should be done with:
options: Soap and running water for at least 15 minutes
questions.concept: Mechanical removal and the lipid-solvent action of soap on the enveloped virus can reduce risk substantially, making this simple step the single most important first-aid measure.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Zoonoses: rabies, plague, leptospirosis, brucellosis
questions.stem: Plague is transmitted from rat to man by:
questions.concept: Blocked flea proventriculus causes regurgitation of bacilli during feeding. Rat fall preceding human cases is the classic warning sign, as fleas leave dying rats to seek human hosts.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Zoonoses: rabies, plague, leptospirosis, brucellosis
questions.stem: Pneumonic plague differs from bubonic in that it:
options: Spreads person to person by droplets and is almost invariably fatal without prompt treatment
questions.concept: It is the only form transmissible between humans, requiring respiratory isolation and prophylaxis of contacts. Plague is a notifiable disease under the International Health Regulations.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Zoonoses: rabies, plague, leptospirosis, brucellosis
questions.stem: Leptospirosis outbreaks in India characteristically follow:
options: Flooding and monsoon rains, with exposure to water contaminated by rodent urine
questions.concept: Paddy field workers, sewage workers and those wading through floodwater are at risk. Doxycycline prophylaxis is used for high-risk exposure during outbreaks.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Zoonoses: rabies, plague, leptospirosis, brucellosis
questions.stem: Brucellosis is prevented in the community principally by:
options: Pasteurisation of milk and vaccination of animals
questions.concept: It is an occupational disease of veterinarians, abattoir workers, farmers and laboratory staff, and is one of the commonest laboratory-acquired infections because of its high infectivity by aerosol.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Zoonoses: rabies, plague, leptospirosis, brucellosis
questions.stem: Anthrax in humans occurs most commonly in which form?
options: Cutaneous, presenting as a painless black eschar
questions.concept: Cutaneous anthrax accounts for over 95% of cases and has low mortality with treatment, while inhalational anthrax carries very high mortality and is the form of bioterrorism concern.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Zoonoses: rabies, plague, leptospirosis, brucellosis
questions.stem: Kyasanur Forest disease, a tick-borne viral haemorrhagic fever, is endemic in:
options: Karnataka and neighbouring Western Ghats districts
questions.concept: Monkeys act as amplifying hosts and Haemaphysalis ticks as vectors, so monkey deaths precede human cases. A vaccine is available for people in affected areas.

questions.subject: PSM (Community Medicine)
questions.topic: Zoonoses: rabies, plague, leptospirosis, brucellosis
questions.stem: The One Health approach to zoonoses recognises that:
options: Human, animal and environmental health are interdependent and require integrated action
questions.concept: Since about 60% of emerging infections are zoonotic, joint surveillance across veterinary, human and wildlife sectors is essential - a lesson reinforced by avian influenza, Nipah and COVID-19.
